acceptance: When a follow-commits review stops because structural inputs are missing, has no evidence paths, and sees no queued evidence and no source change, it ends with a terminal INCOMPLETE outcome within the configured structural wait deadline. The deadline defaults to the reviewer deadline. The process then exits instead of waiting indefinitely, and no approval is recorded.

During that bounded wait the reviewer is not dispatched again, and the controller writes one notice to standard error. The notice names the missing structural inputs reported by the stopped review and explains how to supply them with --evidence.
When qualifying evidence is attached to the live controller during the wait, the review still resumes with that evidence and completes as before.

acceptance_tests.purpose: Runs every native lifecycle case in its own process. This includes the regression in which a review missing structural inputs, with no arrivals, ends INCOMPLETE within a shortened deadline, dispatches the reviewer once and prints a notice naming --evidence. It also includes the unchanged case in which queued evidence arriving during the wait resumes the review to approval.

selection.reason: Small local fix to the native review controller. When follow-commits review stops because structural inputs are missing and no evidence was supplied, the controller waits for queued evidence or source movement with no deadline and no operator notice. The fix bounds that wait by the existing reviewer deadline, prints one notice on standard error that explains how to supply the inputs, and then ends the round as INCOMPLETE. The existing behavior of continuing when evidence arrives is kept. Authentication, public interfaces and published client behavior are unchanged, so this is a bug fix. The focused lifecycle module runs every native lifecycle case in its own process. That includes a new deterministic regression that fails by assertion before the fix and the unchanged evidence-arrival case. The release metadata is checked by the existing release tooling.
